about: A container image that backs up and restores MySQL databases on a schedule.

prs.title: Backups restore the same decimals, fractions of a second and times
prs.broken: Dumps kept only six decimals of floating point numbers, dropped fractions of a second, and shifted TIMESTAMP values by the server's time zone offset on restore.
prs.changed: Numbers are written with all their digits, times keep their fractions, and the dump reads timestamps in the same zone it restores them in.
prs.matters: A restored database holds the same values as the one that was backed up.

prs.title: Binary and bit columns survive a backup and restore
prs.broken: Binary and bit values were written into the dump as raw bytes, so restores failed with a syntax error or brought back wrong values.
prs.changed: These values are now written as escaped binary strings, the same way other binary columns already were.
prs.matters: Backups of tables with hashes, tokens or flags restore correctly.

prs.title: Empty binary values come back empty, not missing
prs.broken: Backups wrote empty binary fields as NULL. After a restore, a value that was empty became missing, which can break apps and constraints that expect a value.
prs.changed: Empty binary values are now written as empty strings, so a restore gives back exactly what was stored.
prs.matters: Backups restore the data as it was.
